classification.classification_note: The staged Capstone source and fix diff match the reported CWE-457: `cs_disasm()` allocates `cs_insn` records without zeroing them, the missing `ARM_t__brkdiv0` metadata row leaves `insn->id` unwritten, and `fill_insn()`'s `OpcodePub` guard falls through before `ARM_post_printer()` reads that stale heap value.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 3-byte witness `03 f9 de` makes `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` open Capstone's Thumb backend, enable detail mode, and pass instruction bytes `f9 de` into `cs_disasm()`. `_Thumb_getInstruction()` reads those bytes as little-endian Thumb16 word `0xdef9`, and the generated Thumb16 decoder table emits internal opcode `ARM_t__brkdiv0`. `cs_disasm()` allocated the destination `cs_insn` array with `cs_mem_malloc` and does not clear `insn_cache->id`. `ARM_get_insn_id()` then looks up `mci.Opcode` in the generated `insns` table built from `ARMMappingInsn.inc`, but the vulnerable table stops at `ARM_tUXTH` and has no row for `ARM_t__brkdiv0`, so the guarded block that should assign `insn->id` and derive `detail->arm.update_flags` is skipped. `_Thumb_getInstruction()` already zeroed `cs_detail`, `MCInst_Init()` started `mci.OpcodePub` at 0, and `ARMInstPrinter.c` has no `MCInst_setOpcodePub()` special case for `t__brkdiv0`; `ARMGenAsmWriter.inc` likewise records public-opcode table entry `0U` for that opcode. As a result, `fill_insn()` sees `MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci) == 0`, skips its last-chance `insn->id` overwrite, and calls `ARM_post_printer()` with `insn->id` still holding the heap bytes from `cs_mem_malloc`. At line 408, the comparison `insn->id == insn_update_flgs[i].id` reads that indeterminate value and MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value. The fix adds the missing `ARM_t__brkdiv0` metadata row to `ARMMappingInsn.inc` and the corresponding operand-access row to `ARMMappingInsnOp.inc`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the two attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the Thumb16 word later decoded as internal opcode `ARM_t__brkdiv0`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly the 3-byte blob `03 f9 de`. Selector byte `0x03` chooses `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }`, and the remaining bytes `f9 de` reach this statement as `code[0..1]`, which `_Thumb_getInstruction()` reads as little-endian Thumb16 word `0xdef9` before the generated decoder table materializes `ARM_t__brkdiv0`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The generated `insns[]` table lacks an `ARM_t__brkdiv0` row, so `insn_find()` returns 0 for the witness opcode and the guarded block that should initialize `insn->id` and `detail->arm.update_flags` is skipped.
root_cause.note: In the vulnerable tree, `ARMMappingInsn.inc` ends at `ARM_tUXTH`; the fix inserts the missing `ARM_t__brkdiv0` row immediately after it and adds a matching operand-access row to `ARMMappingInsnOp.inc`. On the witnessed path that omission leaves `insn->id` as heap garbage from `cs_mem_malloc`, preserves `_Thumb_getInstruction()`'s zero `update_flags` state, and forces the later `fill_insn()` `OpcodePub` guard to be the last chance to overwrite `insn->id` before the sink.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The fallback update-flags scan compares `insn->id` against each static `insn_update_flgs` entry, consuming the still-uninitialized heap value left in `cs_insn.id`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `ARM_post_printer` line 408:43 and says the poisoned value originated at the heap allocation in `cs_disasm` line 836.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant uninitialized state is the `cs_insn.id` field inside the heap-allocated instruction cache. `cs_disasm()` allocates that array with `cs_mem_malloc` and does not zero it, so `insn_cache->id` remains indeterminate until some later mapping or alias path writes it.

parser_admitted.code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
parser_admitted.description: The staged witness has selector byte `0x03`, so `i == 3` and `cs_open()` chooses `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }`. Line 385 has already enabled `CS_OPT_DETAIL`, so line 392 admits the remaining bytes `f9 de` onto the crashing Thumb/ARM parser path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness uses selector byte `0x03` to open the Thumb backend, enables detail mode, and passes the remaining two bytes into `cs_disasm()`.

The Thumb decoder turns `f9 de` into internal opcode `ARM_t__brkdiv0`, but the generated ARM instruction map has no row for that opcode, so `ARM_get_insn_id()` leaves `insn->id` untouched and never overwrites the zero `update_flags` state.
`fill_insn()` checks `MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci)` before calling the post-printer, but `OpcodePub` is still 0 on the `t__brkdiv0` witness path, so the last `insn->id` overwrite is skipped.

Because `update_flags` is still false, `ARM_post_printer()` enters its fallback scan and compares the uninitialized `insn->id` against `insn_update_flgs`, where MSAN reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact selector byte `0x03` makes `i == 3`, so `cs_open()` chooses `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }`. The harness also enables `CS_OPT_DETAIL`, which is required for `ARM_post_printer()` to execute, and passes the remaining bytes `f9 de` into `cs_disasm()`.
Allocates the `cs_insn` cache from heap memory without zeroing it. The first `insn_cache->id` field starts indeterminate and only becomes defined if later code writes a public opcode into it.
Because step 0 enabled detail mode, `cs_disasm()` allocates a `cs_detail` object for this instruction. The Thumb decoder will then zero this record before `ARM_post_printer()` inspects it.

The Thumb decoder zeros the ARM detail record before decoding the instruction. This makes `detail->arm.update_flags` start as `false`, so if later metadata lookup fails to overwrite it, `ARM_post_printer()` will take its fallback update-flags scan.
Source. Reads the attacker-controlled instruction bytes `f9 de` as little-endian Thumb16 word `0xdef9`, the exact word later dispatched through the Thumb16 decoder table.

On the `DecoderTableThumb16` path, the generated decode row at line 7520 (`MCD_OPC_Decode ... // Opcode: t__brkdiv0`) reaches this assignment and materializes internal opcode `ARM_t__brkdiv0` in `mci.Opcode` for the witness word `0xdef9`.

Root cause. The generated `insns[]` table is built from `ARMMappingInsn.inc`, and in the vulnerable tree that included table ends at `ARM_tUXTH` and has no `ARM_t__brkdiv0` row. For this opcode, `insn_find()` returns 0, so the guarded block does not write `insn->id` and does not replace step 3's zero `update_flags` state.

This is the last source-level overwrite point for `insn->id` before the sink. `MCInst_Init()` set `mci->OpcodePub` to 0, the witness opcode remains `ARM_t__brkdiv0`, and neither the explicit `MCInst_setOpcodePub()` special cases in `ARMInstPrinter.c` nor the generated alias/public-opcode path in `ARMGenAsmWriter.inc` supplies a nonzero public ID for this instruction. Therefore `MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci)` is 0 here, line 532 is skipped, and line 536 calls `ARM_post_printer()` with `insn->id` still holding the heap bytes from step 1.

After step 7 calls the post-printer with `insn->id` still untouched, this condition is true because step 3 zeroed the ARM detail struct and step 6 skipped the metadata-derived overwrite. With detail mode already on from step 0, `ARM_post_printer()` enters the fallback loop that consults `insn_update_flgs`.

MSAN sink. The fallback update-flags scan compares `insn->id` against each static table entry, but step 7 passed the same heap bytes from step 1 through `fill_insn()` without any overwrite. MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `ARM_post_printer` line 408:43 and attributes the origin to the `cs_mem_malloc` allocation in `cs_disasm`.

allocation_context.description: The saved MSAN origin stack points to the heap allocation of the `cs_insn` cache at `total = cs_mem_malloc(total_size);`. Because the missing `ARM_t__brkdiv0` mapping row prevents `ARM_get_insn_id()` from writing `insn->id`, the first `cs_insn.id` field remains the indeterminate heap contents from this allocation.

The saved stack is `ARM_post_printer -> fill_insn -> cs_disasm -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; the fine trace now explicitly covers both the skipped `ARM_get_insn_id()` initialization and `fill_insn()`'s false `MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci)` guard before the post-printer read.

format.contract: A 3-byte binary input where byte 0 is exactly `0x03` so `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }` is selected, and bytes 1..2 are exactly `f9 de`, which `_Thumb_getInstruction()` reads as little-endian Thumb16 word `0xdef9` and `DecoderTableThumb16` decodes as internal opcode `ARM_t__brkdiv0`. This GT is grounded only for that exact selector byte and 2-byte instruction witness, not a generalized class of Thumb inputs.
